newsitem.title: FRANCE: French see Pope as out of touch ahead of visit.
newsitem.headline: French see Pope as out of touch ahead of visit.

text.p: The French people believe Pope John Paul is out of touch with modern problems and are indifferent to his planned visit to France next week, a poll showed on Friday.

The IPSOS survey for the weekly Le Point magazine said a majority in this once fervent Roman Catholic nation had a good opinion of the Pope but 70 percent found his answers ill-suited to the problems of the end of the 20th century.
An overwhelming 87 percent disagreed with his opposition to the use of condoms.

The Pope is to tour France from September 19 to 22, visiting Tours, Brittany, Vendee and Reims. Many leftist groups oppose his visit and accuse the centre-right government of violating laws separating church and state by funding the trip.

But 49 percent of those polled said they were indifferent to the visit, the Pope's fifth to a country called "the eldest daughter of the Church" by Catholic traditionalists because of its long ties to Rome.
Only five percent said they felt "fervour" about the visit, slightly fewer than the seven percent who expressed "hostility".
The survey of 1,010 people conducted on August 30 and 31 also found that just 63 percent of French people believe in God.
